content: I assume this will be unanimous since I've been the one advocating to keep it around, would people prefer the Frac typeclass be replaced with a concrete { q : Rat // 0 < q } type? I actually missed that got upstreamed to core in October of last year (after we implemented Frac) and after thinking about Michael's comments some more I think our Frac typeclasses probably don't have that many interesting instances. Would we prefer Qp?

I was thinking today if the following type was even a Frac

inductive SharesOf where
| whole
| partial (root : SharesOf) (N : Nat) (D : Fin N)

(ie. a type which allows fractions to be finitely divided at a certain level) but the totality of addition means this doesn't even fit. Same goes for abstract read permissions and finitely divisible fractions--Iris is built on assumptions that really strongly constrain this type such that anything interesting will have a model in Rat (except reals, but even I don't think that's worth it at this point). Given that Rat is in core now, I propose we kill this darling.

I actually thought about this last week as part of the IsOp PR. The only reason I could think of for keeping Frac is if one wants to support real permissions in addition to rational permissions. But I don't know of an actual use case for this. (I think Viper uses Real permissions since they are better supported in smt solvers, but I am not sure if this applies to Iris / Lean.)
Yea, in your IsOp PR I actually still thought that Rat was in mathlib
As one of the people who implemented it, I would have preferred to use Rat from the beginning, so here’s me saying yes to the proposal.
But please make sure you also get the tactic support first: ring, field_simp, linarith, norm_num and all that. At least some of them are subsumed by grind.
Looks decisive, I will make a PR!
My review on the PR is more a suggestion than anything else. I saw a bunch of projection lemmas which mathlib’s simps attribute generates automatically, so I think it might be worth upstreaming it.
